clue.text: Acquired this Latin style of architecture

parts.note: acquired means got, as in obtained
hic is the Latin word for this

explanation.surface: A remark that someone picked up a classical architectural style.
explanation.definitionFit: Gothic is the medieval building manner of pointed arches and ribbed vaults.

clue.text: Everything that's written up in a poem. The Glad Eye

indicators.note: in places the turned pieces inside the word for a poem

parts.note: an ode is a lyric poem

indicators.note: in a down clue, written up means the pieces read from bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: everything means all
that's, that is, abbreviates to i.e., from Latin id est

explanation.surface: A poem that records everything, followed by the title of a work about flirting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'written up' works because this is a down clue: the pieces read upwards. The Glad Eye is capitalised to look like a title.
explanation.definitionFit: An oeillade is an amorous ogle or wink, the glad eye in old-fashioned slang.

clue.text: Leadership for instance in home reform — Empire State

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation inside the reworked letters
reform means the letters of home are reshaped into a new order

parts.note: e.g. abbreviates exempli gratia, for instance
New York is nicknamed the Empire State, abbreviated NY

explanation.surface: A political slogan about domestic reform and imperial leadership.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Empire State' is the nickname of New York; 'reform' works on 'home' alone, with the abbreviation slipped inside the result.
explanation.definitionFit: Hegemony is dominance or supremacy of one state or group over others.

clue.text: Suffices to support prisoner with fruit preparations

indicators.note: in a down clue, a piece that supports another sits beneath it

parts.note: con is short for convict, a prisoner
suffices means serves, as in will serve the purpose

explanation.surface: Jam-making is enough to keep a prisoner going.
explanation.definitionFit: Conserves are jams or preserves made by cooking fruit with sugar.

clue.text: Binding about punishment this boy received vicariously

definitions.meaning: a cord wound tightly round the end of a rope to stop fraying
beaten in place of a royal prince

explanation.surface: A tale of rope-work and a prince's stand-in taking the beatings.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses share the word: a twine binding round a rope end, and a beating, as in the whipping boy who suffered for a prince.

clue.text: Extremely droopy soup-strainer for an oyster-eater?

definitions.text: Extremely droopy soup-strainer for an oyster-eater?

parts.words: Extremely droopy soup-strainer for an oyster-eater?
parts.note: soup-strainer is slang for a large drooping growth on the upper lip; the oyster-eater is the tusked beast in Lewis Carroll's poem with the Carpenter

explanation.surface: A joke about the facial hair of a creature that eats oysters.
explanation.definitionFit: This style of bushy, downward-hanging upper-lip hair is named after the tusked sea mammal it resembles.

clue.text: Pathfinder putting one in bridge support

indicators.note: putting one thing in another signals that the number goes inside the support
putting one thing in another signals that the number goes inside the support

parts.note: a pier is a pillar holding up a bridge span
taken as written

explanation.surface: An explorer adds a pillar to a bridge.
explanation.definitionFit: A pioneer is a trailblazer who first opens up new ground for others.

clue.text: One member. More's biographer, is out of order

parts.note: one is I, the Roman numeral
MP stands for Member of Parliament
William Roper, son-in-law of Sir Thomas More, wrote his life

explanation.surface: A parliamentarian and a Tudor biographer are judged to be acting unlawfully.
explanation.walkthrough: Thomas More was the Tudor statesman executed by Henry VIII; his son-in-law William Roper wrote the first life of him.
explanation.definitionFit: Something improper is unseemly or not in order.

clue.text: One in the bag for a member of this sporting association

definitions.text: One in the bag for a member of this sporting association

parts.words: One in the bag for a member of this sporting association
parts.note: the implement carried in a caddy's bag shares its name with the society the player belongs to

explanation.surface: A remark about the kit carried by members of a sports society.
explanation.definitionFit: The same phrase names both the stick used to hit the ball on a course and the society that runs that course.

clue.text: Music-maker like Good Queen Bess?

definitions.meaning: a small box-like harpsichord of the sixteenth century
Elizabeth I was the Virgin Queen, so like her means chaste

explanation.surface: An instrument compared to Elizabeth I.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both an early keyboard instrument and the quality of being chaste, Elizabeth I being the Virgin Queen.

clue.text: According to John for instance it's true

definitions.meaning: one of the four New Testament accounts of Christ's life, as in the one according to St John
something taken as absolutely reliable, as in the expression about unquestioned truth

explanation.surface: Someone reports what John said and vouches for it.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a book of Christ's life such as St John's and something accepted as unquestionable truth.

clue.text: Reformed criminal — French link with Father Brown

definitions.meaning: in G K Chesterton's stories the master thief turns honest and becomes Father Brown's friend
a link is an old word for a torch, and this is the French word for one

explanation.surface: A reformed crook from France teams up with a fictional priest-detective.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with Father Brown' places the criminal in Chesterton's detective stories; a link was a torch once carried to light people through the streets.
explanation.definitionFit: Flambeau is the thief who goes straight in the Father Brown tales, and in French the word means a flaming torch.

clue.text: Might Leander's feat be so described in such couplets?

definitions.text: Might Leander's feat be so described in such couplets?

parts.words: Might Leander's feat be so described in such couplets?
parts.note: Leander swam the Hellespont nightly to his lover Hero, so his feat is named after her as well as being brave; rhyming iambic pentameter pairs bear the same name

explanation.surface: A question about how a mythical swimmer's exploit would be written up in verse.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means valiant, and also names the rhymed pentameter couplets, while hinting at Leander's lover Hero.

clue.text: When mob never destroyed parliament in 1605

definitions.text: When mob never destroyed parliament in 1605

indicators.note: destroyed means the letters of mob and never are broken up and rebuilt

explanation.surface: A history-lesson question about the Gunpowder Plot to blow up Parliament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'destroyed' rearranges MOB NEVER. The Gunpowder Plot to blow up the Houses of Parliament was foiled on 5 November 1605, still marked in Britain as Bonfire Night.
explanation.definitionFit: The plot against Parliament in 1605 was due on the fifth of the eleventh month, hence the date of Guy Fawkes Night.

clue.text: Flag raised — deliver speech vanish

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means the word reads upwards, so backwards

parts.note: to flag a floor is to pave it with flagstones
orate means to make a formal speech

explanation.surface: A flag is hoisted, a speech is made, and then everyone disappears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns PAVE into EVAP; 'Flag' looks like a banner but is the verb meaning to lay flagstones.
explanation.definitionFit: To evaporate is to disappear, like water turning to vapour.

clue.text: Missile as alternative weapon for stone-walling cricketer?

definitions.meaning: a piece of masonry thrown in anger, now also a sharp criticism
a stonewalling batsman blocks every ball like a wall, so he might as well carry a bat made of masonry

explanation.surface: A suggestion that a defensive batsman should swap his bat for a missile.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, stonewalling means batting purely defensively, scoring almost nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A brickbat is a lump of masonry used as a missile, and cryptically a bat of brick for a batsman who plays like a wall.

clue.text: Averting trouble for the grape gather

indicators.note: trouble signals that the letters of averting are disturbed into a new order

explanation.surface: Avoiding difficulty for whoever harvests the grapes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trouble for' rearranges AVERTING; the printed 'grape gather' stands for the grape-gatherer.
explanation.definitionFit: A vintager is a worker who picks grapes at harvest time for winemaking.

clue.text: Beat in the third rubber

indicators.note: in signals the letters lie inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A thrashing handed out in the deciding game of a match.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across thiRD RUBber. A rubber is a match of three games in bridge or whist.
explanation.definitionFit: To drub is to thrash or beat soundly.

clue.text: Advertisement indecent? Degenerate

clue.text: What foundations do to lower story

parts.note: lower means under, as in beneath
a story can be a lie, a fib

explanation.surface: A note on how a building's base sits beneath its ground floor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'story' looks like a floor of a building, matching the foundations; here it is a fib.
explanation.definitionFit: Foundations lie beneath a building and support it, which is what underlying means.

clue.text: Kiss by large copper appears untimely

parts.note: OS stands for outsize, a large clothing size
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
late means after the proper time

explanation.surface: A big policeman shows up late for a kiss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' looks like a policeman, but here it is the metal, symbol CU.
explanation.definitionFit: To osculate is a formal or jocular word for to kiss.

clue.text: Cover and extend beyond finished circuit

parts.note: over means ended or finished
a lap is one circuit of a track

explanation.surface: A runner completes a circuit and goes past the line.
explanation.definitionFit: To overlap is to lie partly over something and stick out past it.

clue.text: Exciseman's vessel?

parts.note: a revenue officer's fast patrol boat, and also one who excises, that is, cuts out

explanation.surface: A question about the boat a customs officer uses.
explanation.definitionFit: Revenue officers chased smugglers in light sailing boats of this name, while to excise literally means to cut out.

clue.text: Janus was so insincere

definitions.meaning: the Roman god of doorways is shown with heads looking both ways
deceitful, saying one thing and meaning another

explanation.surface: The Roman god of doorways is accused of hypocrisy.
explanation.definitionFit: Janus literally has a pair of faces, and the word also means hypocritical or deceitful.

clue.text: A phantom about midnight could cause the mind to do so

definitions.text: could cause the mind to do so

indicators.note: about means the ghost goes round the middle letter

parts.note: a bogle is a goblin or ghost in Scots and northern dialect
the middle of the word night is the letter G

explanation.surface: A ghost appearing around midnight would astonish anyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'midnight' is the middle letter of NIGHT, a common crossword trick.
explanation.definitionFit: The mind is said to boggle when it is overwhelmed by something hard to believe.

clue.text: Knowing weight-lifter originally as Daddy-long-legs

parts.note: a crane is a machine for hoisting heavy loads
fly is British slang for sharp or knowing

explanation.surface: A shrewd bodybuilder is likened to a long-legged insect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'weight-lifter' suggests an athlete but is the hoisting machine; FLY, meaning streetwise, follows it though 'Knowing' comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: Daddy-long-legs is the common British name for the long-legged insect of the family Tipulidae.

clue.text: Go and fish in the old way

parts.note: a go is a turn, as in it's your go
a pike is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: Advice to go fishing in the traditional manner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go' looks like a verb but is the noun, a turn in a game.
explanation.definitionFit: A turnpike was a toll road of the 18th and 19th centuries, an old kind of highway.

clue.text: Part of the OT is foreign to her

parts.note: est is French for is
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone claims a section of the Old Testament is alien to a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'foreign' looks like an anagram signal, but it tells you to translate 'is' into French.
explanation.definitionFit: Esther is a book of the Old Testament, named after the Jewish queen of Persia.
